publication: BOTANICA VERIDICA — Architecture of Extreme Plants
purpose: Rule 10 scholarly background citations for established biological, biophysical, and historical constants cited in narrative prose outside live GBIF/iNaturalist/OpenTree API payloads.

citations.context: Sequoia sempervirens canopy height (~100+ m) and cohesion-tension hydraulic lift limit (~115-130 m)
citations.source: Koch, G. W., Sillett, S. C., Jennings, G. M. & Davis, S. D. (2004). The limits to tree height. Nature, 428, 851-854.

citations.context: Dionaea muscipula snap-buckling shell inversion (~100 ms) and ~3 cm trap diameter
citations.source: Forterre, Y., Skotheim, J. M., Dumais, J. & Mahadevan, L. (2005). How the Venus flytrap snaps. Nature, 433, 421-425.

citations.context: Dionaea muscipula two-touch <20 s action potential window and 20-30 cm floral scape height separating pollinators from traps
citations.source: Bohm, J. et al. (2016). The Venus Flytrap Dionaea muscipula Counts Prey-Induced Action Potentials to Induce Sodium Uptake. Current Biology, 26(3), 286-295.

citations.context: Victoria amazonica ~2.5 m giant floating pad diameter and radial girder inspiration for Joseph Paxton's 1851 Crystal Palace
citations.source: Box, F., Erlich, A., Guan, J. H. & Thorogood, C. (2022). Gigantic floating leaves occupy a large surface area at an economical material cost. Science Advances, 8(6), eabg3790.

citations.context: Comparative schematic scale benchmarks (human 1.7 m reference, Ginkgo ~8 cm leaf, Adansonia ~10 m trunk diameter, log10(100/0.03) = 3.5 orders of magnitude, 17th-century Ginkgo transcription by Kaempfer)
